definition_class: D1 source radiated acoustic energy / KE (model-inverted)
numerator: total acoustic energy radiated at the source, one-pole f^-2 spectrum normalised 1-500 Hz
propagation_relation_required: module chain only: explicit source depth z_s (surface-image effect) + KRAKEN adiabatic modes + RAM correction along each bathymetric path, WOA23 month profiles, receiver depth and instrument response; exposure-based scoring
notes: 4 decades. F-35A anchor 2.26e-3 sits 0.65 decades below the top. If z_s is sampled, scale both bounds by eta_F35(z_s)/2.26e-3 (x24 at 2 m, x0.15 at 30 m; 22 Oct values) so the F-35A stays calibrated. Sensitivity variant: 1e-7 to 3e-2.

definition_class: D2 Arons-equivalent in-channel TNT energy / KE (path-blind, end-to-end)
numerator: 4.184e6 J/kg x W, where W solves Arons 1954 for the observed peak pressure at range R
propagation_relation_required: Arons 1954: P_peak = 52.4e6 (R/W^(1/3))^-1.13 Pa with R = source-receiver range; peak pressure (not RMS, not exposure)
notes: Upper bound = F-35A at a favourable site. Lower bound from the 7th-arc site penalty: Duncan & Dall'Osto modelled the MH370 path 20-30 dB below the F-35A path; with P ~ W^0.377 that is a factor 450-9600 in W (own arithmetic), giving 2.2e-8 to 4.7e-7 for an F-35A-like impact; rounded down to 1e-8 to allow slower or blunter impacts. Site and path effects are inside this eta, so it must not be combined with a TL model.

reference: Brown, McFadden, McCormack, Adams & Vida 2026, Icarus 455:117106 (accepted 14 Apr 2026), pp.17-18 of AAM; doi 10.1016/j.icarus.2026.117106
notes: Brown: SOFAR channel at the crash site only 500-700 m deep (Chu & Fan 2024), "may be a higher efficiency than in the open ocean and again should be taken as an upper bound".

numerator: W = 0.0447 kg TNT (own reproduction) x 4.184 MJ/kg = 1.87e5 J
reference: own arithmetic; other thread reported 0.045 kg -> 2.1e-4 (agrees)
notes: If the digitised 1-s RMS peaks (0.31-0.37 Pa, 4-64 Hz) are used instead of 0.7 Pa, the same relation gives 2.4e-5 to 3.8e-5: D2 values depend on the peak definition by nearly a decade.

numerator: total radiated acoustic energy, f^-2 one-pole, 1-500 Hz normalisation
propagation_relation_required: module KRAKEN + RAM correction, GEBCO_2026/WOA23 April path, hard bottom; measured exposure
notes: Depends mainly on assumed source depth (factor 160 between 2 and 30 m). KRAKEN without RAM gives 1.05e-3 at 10 m. Not a published value.

numerator: as above, via peak-to-exposure template ratio from 0.7 Pa
propagation_relation_required: module KRAKEN only (no RAM), hard bottom, 5-40 Hz; template C2
notes: This is the source of "about 1e-4 at 30 m". The 22 Oct re-derivation with measured exposure and RAM gives 3.4e-4 at 30 m.

definition_class: D4 in-band source radiated energy / KE (lower bound of D1)
numerator: radiated energy in 4-64 Hz from observed spectrum + TL
propagation_relation_required: module band-by-band TL (KRAKEN+RAM), observed spectrum shape

definition_class: D3 near-field radiated acoustic energy / KE (measured)
numerator: acoustic energy measured near the impact in a tank
band_Hz: not known from abstract (bubble collapse, likely kHz)
source_depth_m: bubble near surface, first ~0.6 m (2 ft) of travel
propagation_relation_required: free-field/tank near field; to use, pair with an explicit source model (spectrum, depth, directivity) and full TL; never with Arons
reference: Leslie 1964 JASA 36:1138 (abstract); Brown, McFadden, McCormack, Adams & Vida 2026, Icarus 455:117106 (accepted 14 Apr 2026) p.7
read_in_primary: abstract only; no legitimate copy found
role_in_prior: upper bound of PRIOR-A (total, all bands)
notes: Near-field acoustic energy, NOT coupling into the deep sound channel. Most of it is probably above the IMS band, so the in-band fraction for an airliner is lower.

numerator: water-column acoustic energy from line-source measurements
source acoustic energy below 100 Hz after Bellhop TL + terminus reflection
propagation_relation_required: Bellhop ray TL with terminus reflection (Glowacki & Deane 2020)

reference: Glowacki et al. 2015 GRL 42:804 (via Glowacki & Deane 2020)
notes: Same physics, different propagation relation, ~3 decades lower than ICE-2020: direct evidence that eta values do not carry over between propagation relations.

reference: Brown, McFadden, McCormack, Adams & Vida 2026, Icarus 455:117106 (accepted 14 Apr 2026) Table A.4
role_in_prior: exclude for impacts; shows site/path scatter of D2 (3.5 decades)

notes: Different denominator (P V, not KE). Do not mix with impact prior.
Suggested implosion prior: log-uniform 2e-3 to 0.18 of P V.
